words.ex: He values education very much.
words.ex_cn: 他非常重视教育。
words.en: Education is the process of teaching and learning, especially in a school or college, or the knowledge that you get from this.

words.ex: He finished his schooling at age 18.
words.ex_cn: 他18岁时完成了学业。
words.en: Schooling is the education that a person receives at school.

words.ex: Good parenting helps children grow happily.
words.ex_cn: 良好的育儿有助于孩子快乐成长。
words.en: Parenting is the activity of bringing up and looking after children.

words.ex: He taught math in primary school.
words.ex_cn: 他在小学教数学。
words.en: A primary school is a school for children between the ages of about five and eleven.

words.ex: He will replace the broken chair.
words.ex_cn: 他将代替这把坏掉的椅子。
words.en: If one thing or person replaces another, the first is used or acts instead of the second.

words.tr:
v. 补充；与…相辅相成；
n. 补足物；补语；余角；
words.ex: The red scarf complements her blue coat.
words.ex_cn: 这条红围巾补充了她的蓝外套。
words.en: To complement something means to make it complete or perfect by adding something to it.

words.ex: Parents should instil good habits in children.
words.ex_cn: 父母应该逐渐向孩子灌输良好的习惯。
words.en: If you instil an idea or feeling in someone, especially over a period of time, you make them think it or feel it.

words.ex: He imparts knowledge to his students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天向学生传授知识。
words.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality.

words.tr: n. 反复灌输；谆谆教诲；
words.ex: The inculcation of good habits starts in childhood.
words.ex_cn: 好习惯的反复灌输从童年就开始了。
words.en: The act of inculcating; teaching or impressing upon the mind by frequent instruction or repetition.

words.ex: Farmers cultivate rice in the fields.
words.ex_cn: 农民在田里种植水稻。
words.en: To cultivate land means to prepare it and grow crops on it. To cultivate a particular quality, skill, or attitude means to try hard to develop it and make it stronger.

words.ex: Exercise can enhance your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提高你的健康。
words.en: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

words.ex: Good teachers motivate students to learn.
words.ex_cn: 好老师激励学生学习。
words.en: To motivate someone means to provide them with a reason for doing something, especially something that requires effort.

words.ex: The bright light stimulated her eyes.
words.ex_cn: 强烈的光线刺激了她的眼睛。
words.en: To stimulate something means to encourage it to begin or develop further.

words.tr:
v. （使）获得；
adj. 安全的；稳定的；
words.ex: He worked hard to secure a job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以获得一份工作。
words.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

words.tr:
v. 打破；打断；
n. 休息；中断；破裂；
words.ex: He broke the glass by accident.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心打破了玻璃。
words.en: If you break something, you cause it to separate into two or more pieces, often in a way that is irreparable.

words.ex: He adapted to the new school quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就适应了新学校。
words.en: To make suitable to or fit for a specific use or situation.

words.tr: v. 完成；实现；达到；获得；
words.ex: He worked hard to achieve his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以完成他的目标。
words.en: To achieve something means to reach a particular goal or result through effort, skill, or courage.

words.ex: He acquired a new skill last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了一项新技能。
words.en: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.

words.ex: He excels in math.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长数学。
words.en: To be exceptionally good at or proficient in an activity or subject.

words.tr:
adj. 学术的；
n. 大学教师；学者；
words.ex: He published an academic paper on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇关于气候变化的学术论文。
words.en: relating to education, especially at college or university level

words.ex: He has a talent for playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他有弹钢琴的才能。
words.en: If someone has a talent for something, they have a natural ability to do it well.

words.ex: The well-bred child said thank you politely.
words.ex_cn: 这个有教养的孩子礼貌地说了谢谢。
words.en: Someone who is well-bred has good manners and has been well brought up.

words.ex: The two colors distinguish the two teams.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色使两个队伍有所不同。
words.en: If you can distinguish one thing from another, you can see or understand how they are different.

words.tr: v. 增加；引起；筹募；提起；养育；
words.ex: The company will raise wages next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将提高工资。
words.en: To raise something means to move it to a higher position or to increase it in amount or level.

words.tr:
n. 纪律；学科；科目；训练；惩戒；
v. 约束自己；
words.ex: The teacher enforced discipline in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师在教室里维持纪律。
words.en: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

words.tr:
n. 意义；感知；理解力；知觉；
v. 感觉到；觉察出；意识到；
words.ex: The story has no sense.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事没有意义。
words.en: A sense is a feeling or awareness about something, or a physical ability such as sight, hearing, touch, taste, or smell.

words.tr:
n. 特点；特性；
adj. 典型的；特有的；
words.ex: Honesty is a key characteristic of a good friend.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一个好朋友的关键特点。
words.en: A characteristic is a quality or feature that is typical of someone or something.

words.tr:
adj. 道德的；道义上的；
n. 寓意；
words.ex: It is a moral duty to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 说实话是一种道德责任。
words.en: Concerned with the principles of right and wrong behavior and the goodness or badness of human character.

words.tr:
adj. 智力的；
n. 知识分子；
words.ex: He is an intellectual person who loves solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱解决数学问题的智力型人。
words.en: An intellectual is someone who spends a lot of time studying and thinking about complicated ideas.

words.tr:
n. 潜力；
adj. 潜在的；
words.ex: The young athlete shows great potential.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻运动员展现出巨大的潜力。
words.en: If you say that someone or something has potential, you mean that they have the necessary abilities or qualities to become successful or useful in the future.

words.ex: Babies have an innate ability to cry.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿生来就有哭泣的能力。
words.en: An innate quality or ability is one that you were born with, not one you have learned.

words.ex: His nature is kind and patient.
words.ex_cn: 他的本性是善良且有耐心的。
words.en: Nature refers to the physical world and everything in it that is not made by people, including plants, animals, mountains, oceans, stars, etc. It can also refer to the basic or inherent features, character, or qualities of something.

words.tr:
n. 教养；养育；培育；
v. 培养；
words.ex: Her parents gave her good nurture.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母给了她良好的教养。
words.en: To nurture someone or something is to care for and encourage their growth or development.

words.tr: adj. 多方面的；有多种技能的；
words.ex: He is a versatile player who can play many positions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名多方面的运动员，能打多个位置。
words.en: Able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.

words.ex: His competence in math helped him solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学方面的能力帮助他解决了这个问题。
words.en: Competence is the ability to do something well or efficiently.

words.ex: He will misguide you with wrong advice.
words.ex_cn: 他会用错误的建议误导你。
words.en: If you are misguided by someone or something, you are led to believe something that is not true or to do something that is wrong or not suitable.

words.ex: He has a natural aptitude for math.
words.ex_cn: 他天生有数学天赋。
words.en: An aptitude is a natural ability to do something.

words.tr: n. 地平线；思想等的范围；眼界；
words.ex: The sun set below the horizon.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在地平线以下落山。
words.en: The horizon is the line at which the earth's surface and the sky appear to meet.

words.tr: adv. 社会上；交际上；以社会方式地；
words.ex: He is socially active in his community.
words.ex_cn: 他在社会上积极参与社区活动。
words.en: In a way that relates to society or its organization.

words.ex: He joins extracurricular activities after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后参加课外活动。
words.en: Extracurricular activities are those that fall outside the realm of the normal curriculum of school or university education, performed by students. Extracurricular activities exist at all levels of education, from 4th-6th, junior high/high school, college and university education.

words.ex: The scope of this project includes three cities.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的范围包括三个城市。
words.en: The range of one's perceptions, thoughts, or actions.

words.ex: He protects the environment by recycling.
words.ex_cn: 他通过回收利用来保护环境。
words.en: The environment is the natural world in which people, animals, and plants live.

words.ex: He goes to nursery school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上上幼儿园。
words.en: A nursery school is a school for children between the ages of about two and five.

words.tr: v. 互相作用；互相影响；交流；沟通；
words.ex: The two chemicals interact when mixed.
words.ex_cn: 这两种化学物质混合时会互相作用。
words.en: If people interact with each other, they communicate or work together.

words.tr: n. 学习；学问； v. 学习；“learn”的现在分词；
words.ex: Learning takes time and practice.
words.ex_cn: 学习需要时间和练习。
words.en: The acquisition of knowledge or skills through study, experience, or being taught.

words.ex: The teacher gave clear instruction on how to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了如何解决这个问题的明确教授。
words.en: Detailed information telling how something should be done, operated, or assembled.

words.ex: The teacher will enlighten the students about the truth.
words.ex_cn: 老师将向学生们阐明真相。
words.en: To enlighten someone means to give them more knowledge and greater understanding about something.

words.ex: Her story inspires me to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 她的故事激励我更加努力。
words.en: If someone or something inspires you to do something new or unusual, they make you want to do it.

words.ex: He spooned sugar into his tea.
words.ex_cn: 他用勺子把糖舀进茶里。
words.en: To use a spoon to scoop or serve something; to cuddle closely with someone.

words.tr: phrase. 集中于； 专心于
words.ex: He must concentrate on his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他必须专心做作业。
words.en: To direct all your attention and effort towards a particular activity, subject, or problem.

words.ex: His preoccupation with video games made him ignore his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏的全神贯注让他忽略了作业。
words.en: If you have a preoccupation with something or someone, you think or worry about them very often and they are the main focus of your attention.

words.ex: The school banned corporal punishment last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年学校禁止了体罚。
words.en: Physical punishment intended to correct or punish a person's behavior.

words.ex: The foundation gives money to poor students.
words.ex_cn: 这个基金会向贫困学生提供资金。
words.en: The foundation of something such as a belief or way of life is the things on which it is based.

words.ex: His perception of the sound was very sharp.
words.ex_cn: 他对声音的感知非常敏锐。
words.en: Your perception of something is the way that you think about it or the impression you have of it.

words.ex: He listened to his conscience and told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他听从了良心，说出了真相。
words.en: Your conscience is the part of your mind that tells you whether what you are doing is right or wrong.

words.tr:
n. 婴儿；
adj. 初期的；
words.ex: The infant is sleeping in the crib.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在婴儿床里睡觉。
words.en: An infant is a baby or very young child.

words.tr:
n. 方法；接近；靠近；路径；
v. 接近；靠近；临近；处理；
words.ex: He used a new approach to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一种新方法来解决问题。
words.en: To come near or nearer to something or someone in distance or time.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.ex: He bullies his little brother every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都欺负他的弟弟。
words.en: To bully someone means to use your strength or power to hurt or frighten them, often forcing them to do something they do not want to do.

words.ex: In essence, he is a kind person.
words.ex_cn: 本质上，他是一个善良的人。
words.en: You use in essence to emphasize that you are talking about the most important or central aspect of an idea, situation, or event.

words.ex: The effectiveness of the new medicine was proven in trials.
words.ex_cn: 这种新药的有效性在试验中得到了证实。
words.en: The ability to produce a desired or intended result.

words.tr: v. 要价；指控；“charge”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 充了电的（带电的）；引起强烈感情的；
words.ex: The shop charged $50 for the shirt.
words.ex_cn: 这家店给这件衬衫要价50美元。
words.en: If a situation or atmosphere is charged, it is filled with emotion and therefore exciting or tense. If someone is charged with a crime, they are officially accused of it.

words.tr: adv. 严重地；批评地；危急地；
words.ex: The patient is critically ill.
words.ex_cn: 病人病情严重。
words.en: In a way that involves the objective analysis and judgment of the merits and faults of a work of literature, music, or art.

words.ex: He was unfit for the job because he lacked experience.
words.ex_cn: 他因缺乏经验而不合格。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is unfit for a particular purpose or job, you are criticizing them because they are not good enough for that purpose or job.

words.ex: The company plans to enlarge its office space.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划扩大其办公空间。
words.en: To make something bigger or more extensive.

words.ex: The shopkeeper will evaluate the old watch.
words.ex_cn: 店主将估价这块旧手表。
words.en: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.

words.tr:
adj. 迟钝的；弱智的；智力发育迟缓的
v. 延迟；弄慢；使耽误；“retard”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was called retarded by some kids at school.
words.ex_cn: 他被学校的一些孩子叫做迟钝的。
words.en: Less advanced in mental, physical, or social development than is usual for one's age.

words.ex: He is a multifaceted person who can sing, paint, and code.
words.ex_cn: 他是个多方面的人，会唱歌、绘画和编程。
words.en: Having many facets or aspects.

words.tr: n. 需优先考虑的事；优先权；
words.ex: Homework is my top priority.
words.ex_cn: 作业是我最需要优先考虑的事。
words.en: If something is a priority, it is the most important thing you have to do or deal with, or must be done or dealt with before everything else you have to do.

words.ex: This decision is pivotal for the company's future.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来至关重要。
words.en: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something else.

words.ex: The truck suffered an overload and broke down.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车因超载而抛锚了。
words.en: To load or burden someone or something excessively.

words.tr: adj. 固有的；内在的；本身的；
words.ex: Honesty is an intrinsic part of her character.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是她性格中固有的部分。
words.en: belonging to a thing by its very nature

words.tr: adj. 无忧无虑的；轻松愉快的；
words.ex: The children played carefree in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里无忧无虑地玩耍。
words.en: If you are carefree, you have no worries or responsibilities, and you are happy and relaxed.

words.ex: He has self-confidence when he speaks in public.
words.ex_cn: 他当众讲话时很有自信。
words.en: Self-confidence is the belief in one's own abilities and judgment.

words.ex: Children develop cognitive skills as they grow.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在成长过程中发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognitive means relating to the mental process involved in knowing, learning, and understanding things.

words.ex: His plan is based on a presupposition that everyone will agree.
words.ex_cn: 他的计划基于一个所有人都会同意的假设。
words.en: A presupposition is something that you assume to be true, especially something which you must assume is true in order to continue with a line of argument or a course of action.

words.tr: phrase. 文科；人文科学（包括语言、哲学、历史、文学、艺术等学科）
words.ex: He majors in liberal arts at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学主修文科。
words.en: The liberal arts are academic subjects such as history, literature, and languages, as distinct from professional and technical subjects.

words.ex: It is worthwhile to learn a new language.
words.ex_cn: 学习一门新语言是值得的。
words.en: If something is worthwhile, it is enjoyable or useful enough to make the effort or money spent on it seem reasonable.

words.ex: The framework of the house is made of wood.
words.ex_cn: 房子的骨架是木制的。
words.en: A framework is a particular set of rules, ideas, or beliefs which you use in order to deal with problems or to decide what to do.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；基本的；本质的；
words.ex: Water is essential for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必需的。
words.en: Something that is essential is extremely important or absolutely necessary to a particular subject, situation, or activity.

words.ex: The scientist made a breakthrough in cancer research.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家在癌症研究中取得了突破。
words.en: A breakthrough is a significant development or achievement that helps to solve a problem or improve a situation.

words.ex: The invention of the internet changed our era.
words.ex_cn: 互联网的发明改变了我们的时代。
words.en: An era is a period of time that is considered as a single unit because of a particular characteristic or event.

words.ex: This school has technological labs for students.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校为学生配备了科技实验室。
words.en: Technological means relating to or involving technology.

words.tr:
n. 发展；进步；提前；
adj. 预先的；在前的；
v. 前进；发展；提前；
words.ex: The advance of technology has changed our lives.
words.ex_cn: 科技的发展改变了我们的生活。
words.en: If you advance a cause, interest, or claim, you support it and help it to succeed.

words.tr: phrase. 迅速地；飞快地；大步地（用于形容进展或增长非常迅速）
words.ex: His English is improving by leaps and bounds.
words.ex_cn: 他的英语正在飞速进步。
words.en: If something increases or improves by leaps and bounds, it does so very quickly and to a great extent.

words.tr: phrase. 扫除；清除；彻底消除
words.ex: The heavy rain may sweep away the small bridge.
words.ex_cn: 大雨可能会冲走这座小桥。
words.en: To remove or eliminate completely and suddenly.

words.tr: adj. 互相依赖的；相倚的；
words.ex: The two countries are interdependent in trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上互相依赖。
words.en: If two or more things are interdependent, they depend on each other.

words.ex: The new machine improves the efficiency of production.
words.ex_cn: 这台新机器提高了生产的效率。
words.en: Efficiency is the ability to do something or produce something without wasting materials, time, or energy.

words.ex: Graduating from high school was a big milestone for him.
words.ex_cn: 从高中毕业对他来说是一个重要的事件。
words.en: A milestone is a significant event or stage in the development of something.

words.ex: The earthquake caused tremendous damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了巨大的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tremendous, you mean that they are very great in amount, extent, or intensity.

words.ex: He works hard to keep pace with his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习以跟上同学的步伐。
words.en: To move or progress at the same rate as someone or something else.

words.tr: v. 重塑；改造；给…以新形态
words.ex: He wants to reshape his life after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他想在事故后重新塑造自己的生活。
words.en: To reshape something means to change its form or structure, often in order to improve it.

words.ex: The view from the mountain is breathtaking.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色令人惊叹。
words.en: If you say that something is breathtaking, you mean that it is extremely beautiful or amazing.

words.ex: The number of stars in the sky is incalculable.
words.ex_cn: 天空中的星星数量是无数的。
words.en: If something is incalculable, it cannot be calculated or measured because it is so great.

words.tr:
adj. 依靠的；依赖的；
n. 受赡养者；
words.ex: The child is dependent on his parents for food.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子依靠父母提供食物。
words.en: A dependent person or thing is one that needs the support of another person or thing in order to exist or be successful.

words.tr: n. 必然性；不可避免性
words.ex: The inevitability of change is clear.
words.ex_cn: 变化的不可避免性是明显的。
words.en: The quality of being certain to happen and unable to be avoided or prevented.

words.ex: He positively believes in his dream.
words.ex_cn: 他积极地相信自己的梦想。
words.en: In a positive manner; with certainty.

words.ex: He responded negatively to the proposal.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个提议持消极态度。
words.en: In a manner that is negative or pessimistic.

words.ex: He felt intense pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他感到剧烈的疼痛。
words.en: If you describe an activity as intense, you mean that it is very serious and concentrated, and often involves doing a great deal in a short time.

words.tr: adj. 虚拟的；几乎的；实际上的；事实上的；
words.ex: He played a virtual game on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他在电脑上玩了一个虚拟游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as virtual, you mean that it is so nearly true that for most purposes it can be regarded as true.

words.ex: He is an addict who cannot stop smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他是个无法戒烟的瘾君子。
words.en: An addict is someone who is unable to stop taking harmful drugs, or someone who is very interested in something and spends a lot of time doing it.

words.ex: He sat with good posture at the desk.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在书桌前，姿势端正。
words.en: Your posture is the way in which you hold your body when you are standing or sitting.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.ex: The worker had long exposure to loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 这名工人长期暴露在噪音中。
words.en: The condition of being exposed to something, especially to something harmful or unpleasant.

words.ex: They will liberate the prisoners tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天会释放这些囚犯。
words.en: To liberate a place or the people in it means to free them from the political or military control of another country, area, or group of people.

words.ex: The long silence caused alienation between them.
words.ex_cn: 长久的沉默导致了他们之间的离间。
words.en: Alienation refers to the state or experience of being isolated from a group or an activity to which one should belong or in which one should be involved.

words.ex: The cities are geographically far apart.
words.ex_cn: 这些城市在地理上相距很远。
words.en: In terms of geography or physical location.

words.ex: He works in telecommunication.
words.ex_cn: 他在电信行业工作。
words.en: Telecommunication is the technology of sending signals, images, and messages over long distances by telephone, radio, television, or satellite.

words.tr:
n. 代用品；代替物；
v. 替代；
words.ex: Honey is a good substitute for sugar.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是糖的良好代用品。
words.en: A substitute is something or someone that takes the place or function of another.

words.ex: The overuse of plastic bags harms the environment.
words.ex_cn: 塑料袋的滥用对环境有害。
words.en: To use something too much or too often.

words.tr: phrase. 有权使用；有机会接近
words.ex: He has access to the library after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后可以使用图书馆。
words.en: The ability or right to approach, enter, or make use of something.

words.tr:
n. 文本；课文；
v. 发短信；
words.ex: He read the text carefully.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细阅读了文本。
words.en: Text refers to any written material, especially the main body of a book or other piece of writing, as distinct from illustrations, notes, or appendices.

words.tr: adj. 选择性的；精挑细选的；
words.ex: He is selective about what he eats.
words.ex_cn: 他对吃的东西很挑剔。
words.en: If you are selective, you choose things carefully, for example, the things that you buy or do.

words.ex: The river is dirty because of pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这条河因为污染而变得肮脏。
words.en: Pollution is the process of making air, water, soil, etc. dirty and not safe or suitable to use.

words.ex: The river is contaminated by factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这条河被工厂废料污染了。
words.en: To contaminate something means to make it impure or polluted by contact or mixture with something unclean or harmful.

words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.tr:
n. 垃圾；废物；浪费；
v. 浪费；白费；糟蹋；
adj. 荒芜的；废弃的；
words.ex: The children threw waste into the bin.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们把垃圾扔进了垃圾桶。
words.en: If you waste something such as time, money, or energy, you use too much of it doing something that is not important or necessary, or you do not use it in a sensible way.

words.ex: This park is an ecological habitat for many birds.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园是许多鸟类的生态栖息地。
words.en: Relating to or concerned with the relation of living organisms to one another and to their physical surroundings.

words.ex: The forest is a healthy ecosystem.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林是一个健康的生态系统。
words.en: An ecosystem is a complex network or interconnected system, especially one that involves a community of living organisms in conjunction with their environment.

words.ex: The extinction of dinosaurs happened millions of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 恐龙的灭绝发生在数百万年前。
words.en: The state or process of a species, family, or larger group being or becoming extinct.

words.ex: The city cleaned the sewage from the streets.
words.ex_cn: 城市清理了街道上的污水。
words.en: Sewage is waste matter such as faeces or dirty water from homes and factories, which flows away through sewers.

words.ex: He used a disposable cup for his coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一次性杯子喝咖啡。
words.en: Something that is disposable is intended to be thrown away after use.

words.tr:
v. 利用；
n. 马具；
words.ex: We must harness the power of the sun.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须利用太阳的能量。
words.en: A harness is a set of straps which fit under a person's arms and fasten round their body in order to keep a piece of equipment in place or to prevent the person moving from a place.

words.tr:
n. 废墟；
v. 破坏；
words.ex: The old temple is now a ruin.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙现在已成为废墟。
words.en: Ruin means the physical destruction or disintegration of something or the state of disintegrating or being destroyed.

words.ex: The bag is biodegradable.
words.ex_cn: 这个袋子是可生物降解的。
words.en: A substance or chemical that is biodegradable can be decomposed by bacteria or other living organisms, and therefore does not pollute the environment.

words.tr:
v. 耗尽；用完；使筋疲力尽
n. 排气管；废气
words.ex: The long hike exhausted him.
words.ex_cn: 这次漫长的徒步旅行让他筋疲力尽。
words.en: If something exhausts you, it makes you so tired, either physically or mentally, that you have no energy left.

words.ex: The ozone layer protects us from the sun's harmful rays.
words.ex_cn: 臭氧层保护我们免受太阳有害射线的伤害。
words.en: The ozone layer is a layer in the Earth's stratosphere that contains a high concentration of ozone (O3) molecules, which absorb most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

words.ex: He used up all the water.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的水都用完了。
words.en: To consume or exhaust something completely.

words.ex: The car consumes a lot of gas.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车消耗很多汽油。
words.en: To consume something means to eat or drink it, or to use it up in some way.

words.tr:
n. 释放；发布；
v. 释放；发布；
words.ex: The release of the prisoner made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯的释放让每个人都高兴。
words.en: To release something means to let it go or to allow it to be free, or to make something available to the public.

words.ex: The factory reduces emission to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 工厂减少排放以保护环境。
words.en: An emission is the production and discharge of something, especially gas or radiation.

words.ex: The exploitation of natural resources helps the economy grow.
words.ex_cn: 自然资源的开发有助于经济发展。
words.en: The action or fact of treating someone unfairly in order to benefit from their work, or the utilization of something for profit or gain.

words.ex: The chemicals are hazardous to health.
words.ex_cn: 这些化学物质对健康有危险。
words.en: Something that is hazardous is dangerous, especially to people's health or safety.

words.ex: The pollution caused the degradation of the river.
words.ex_cn: 污染导致了河流的恶化。
words.en: The process by which something is reduced in quality, value, or status.

words.tr: n. 采伐森林；森林开伐；
words.ex: Deforestation is killing many animals.
words.ex_cn: 采伐森林正在杀死许多动物。
words.en: The act of cutting down or burning all the trees in an area.

words.tr: adj. 可更新的；可再生的；
words.ex: Solar energy is a renewable resource.
words.ex_cn: 太阳能是一种可更新的资源。
words.en: A renewable resource is a natural resource which will replenish to replace the portion depleted by usage and consumption, either through natural reproduction or other recurring processes in a finite amount of time in a human time scale.

words.ex: The deterioration of the road made driving dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 道路的恶化使驾驶变得危险。
words.en: The process of becoming progressively worse.

words.ex: The damage to the environment is irreversible.
words.ex_cn: 对环境的破坏是不可逆转的。
words.en: If a change is irreversible, it cannot be changed back to how it was before.

words.tr: n. 包装；装箱；包装物； v. “package”的现在分词；
words.ex: The packaging of the gift was very beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 这份礼物的包装非常漂亮。
words.en: The materials in which goods are wrapped or packed, especially commercially.

words.tr: phrase. 处理好；处置掉；除掉
words.ex: Please dispose of the trash before you leave.
words.ex_cn: 请在离开前处理好垃圾。
words.en: To get rid of something that you no longer want or need.

words.tr: adj. 该受责备的；应受谴责的
words.ex: He is blameworthy for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他因这个错误而应受责备。
words.en: If someone or something is blameworthy, they deserve to be blamed for something bad that has happened.

words.ex: The soil degrades over time without proper care.
words.ex_cn: 如果没有适当照料，土壤会逐渐退化。
words.en: If something degrades or is degraded, it becomes worse in quality, or weaker in power or status.

words.tr:
n. 地址；演讲；
v. 解决；向…讲话；
words.ex: Please write your address on the form.
words.ex_cn: 请把你的地址写在表格上。
words.en: The particulars of the place where someone lives or an organization is situated; a formal speech delivered to an audience.

words.tr:
v. 保存；保护；保持；
n. （某群体）专有的活动；
words.ex: She preserves fresh fruit by making jam.
words.ex_cn: 她通过做果酱来保存新鲜水果。
words.en: To preserve something means to maintain it in its original or existing state.

words.tr: n. 替代选择；替代选择（alternative 的复数）；
words.ex: We need to find better alternatives to plastic.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要找到比塑料更好的替代选择。
words.en: An alternative is something that you can choose to do or use instead of something else.

words.tr:
v. 发射；发起；启动；
n. 发射；投掷；启动；
words.ex: They will launch a rocket tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将发射一枚火箭。
words.en: To launch something means to send it into the air, space, or water, especially with a lot of force or effort, or to start an activity, event, or project.

words.ex: We need sustainable energy to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要可持续的能源来保护环境。
words.en: If something is sustainable, it can be maintained or continued at a certain rate or level without causing damage or depletion of resources.

words.ex: He uses a low-carbon bike to work.
words.ex_cn: 他骑一辆低碳自行车去上班。
words.en: Relating to or involving a reduced amount of carbon emissions, especially carbon dioxide.

words.ex: The forest has high biodiversity.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林生物多样性很高。
words.en: Biodiversity refers to the variety of life in the world or in a particular habitat or ecosystem.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.ex: The desert has a harsh climate.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的气候非常严酷。
words.en: If you describe something as harsh, you mean that it is extremely difficult and unpleasant to live in, do, or experience, especially because it is very cold, hot, or violent.

words.ex: The fence safeguards the garden from animals.
words.ex_cn: 围栏保护花园免受动物侵扰。
words.en: A safeguard is a measure taken to protect someone or something from potential harm or danger.

words.ex: We recycle plastic bottles every week.
words.ex_cn: 我们每周回收塑料瓶。
words.en: To recycle means to process used materials so that they can be used again.

words.ex: He lost consciousness after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后失去了意识。
words.en: The state of being aware of and able to think about oneself, one's surroundings, and one's experiences.

words.ex: His attainment of the goal took many years.
words.ex_cn: 他达到这个目标花了多年时间。
words.en: The act of achieving something, especially through effort; a skill or accomplishment that has been achieved.

words.ex: The pandemic caused many schools to close.
words.ex_cn: 这场流行病导致许多学校关闭。
words.en: A pandemic is an occurrence of a disease that affects many people over a wide area.

words.ex: His egregious mistake cost the team the game.
words.ex_cn: 他严重的错误让球队输掉了比赛。
words.en: An egregious error or failure is extremely bad and noticeable.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.ex: He built a successful career in medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他在医学领域建立了成功的事业。
words.en: A career is the job or series of jobs that you do during your working life, especially if you continue to get better jobs and earn more money.

words.ex: His profession is a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他的职业是教师。
words.en: A profession is a type of job that requires advanced education or training.

words.tr: vi. （在家里通过使用与工作单位连接的计算机终端）远距离工作
words.ex: He telecommutes from home on Fridays.
words.ex_cn: 他在周五从家远程工作。
words.en: To work from home, communicating with your office by telephone or using the internet.

words.tr: adj. 有报酬的；有利益的；
words.ex: He took a remunerative job to support his family.
words.ex_cn: 他找了一份有报酬的工作来养家。
words.en: providing payment; profitable

words.ex: He is on probation for one year.
words.ex_cn: 他被判缓刑一年。
words.en: Probation is a period of time during which someone who has committed a crime has to behave well and not commit any more crimes in order to avoid being sent to prison.

words.ex: The employee arrived at work early.
words.ex_cn: 这位雇员早早到达了工作地点。
words.en: An employee is a person who is paid to work for an organization or for another person.

words.tr: phrase. 失业的；没有工作的
words.ex: He is out of work after the factory closed.
words.ex_cn: 工厂关闭后，他失业了。
words.en: If someone is out of work, they do not have a job.

words.ex: He will undertake a new project next month.
words.ex_cn: 他下个月将从事一个新项目。
words.en: To undertake a task or job means to start doing it and accept responsibility for it.

words.tr:
n. 法官；裁判；
v. 判断；评判；
words.ex: The judge announced the verdict in court.
words.ex_cn: 法官在法庭上宣布了判决。
words.en: A judge is a person who has the authority to decide questions brought before a court of law. To judge means to form an opinion or conclusion about something.

words.tr: adj. 单调乏味的；毫无变化的；
words.ex: The work is monotonous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作单调乏味。
words.en: Something that is monotonous is very boring because it has a regular, repeated pattern which never changes.

words.tr:
n. 奖励；报酬；
v. 奖励；回报；
words.ex: He got a reward for winning the contest.
words.ex_cn: 他因赢得比赛而得到了奖励。
words.en: Something given or received in return for a deed or service rendered.

words.tr:
n. 同辈；同等的人；
v. 凝视；
words.ex: He feels comfortable talking to his peers.
words.ex_cn: 他觉得和同辈交谈很自在。
words.en: A peer is someone who is equal to another in abilities, qualifications, age, background, or social status. As a verb, to peer means to look keenly or with difficulty at someone or something.

words.ex: He is a veteran player with many years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位经验丰富的老练球员。
words.en: A veteran is someone who has a lot of experience in a particular field or activity, especially in the armed forces.

words.ex: The faculty of engineering has many labs.
words.ex_cn: 工程学院有许多实验室。
words.en: A faculty is a group of departments in a university or college that specialize in a particular subject or group of subjects, or the teachers in such a group.

words.ex: The rifle has a 5.56 mm caliber.
words.ex_cn: 这把步枪的口径是5.56毫米。
words.en: The caliber of something or someone is their quality, especially when this is high.

words.ex: The survey asks about your gender.
words.ex_cn: 这个调查询问你的性别。
words.en: Gender is the state of being male or female, especially when considered with reference to social and cultural differences, not just biological ones.

words.ex: He noticed the discrimination between the two prices.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了两个价格之间的区别。
words.en: The unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, age, or sex.

words.tr:
adj. 相等的；同等的；
v. 等于；比得上；
words.ex: Two plus two is equal to four.
words.ex_cn: 二加二等于四。
words.en: If two things are equal, or if one thing is equal to another, they are the same in size, number, standard, or value.

words.ex: The new policy is for the promotion of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策是为了促进清洁能源。
words.en: A promotion is a move to a more important job or rank in a company or organization.

words.ex: The new policy improves worker mobility.
words.ex_cn: 新政策提高了工人的流动性。
words.en: The ability to move or be moved freely and easily.

words.ex: He gave a reasonable answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个合理的回答。
words.en: Fair and sensible; not excessive or extreme.

words.tr:
adj. 客观的；
n. 目标；目的；
words.ex: He gave an objective opinion about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影给出了一个客观的看法。
words.en: An objective is something that you plan to do or achieve.

words.ex: The meeting was fruitful and solved many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议富有成效，解决了许多问题。
words.en: Producing good or helpful results; productive.

words.tr:
n. 展示；陈列；
v. 展示；陈列；
words.ex: The store has a big display of new phones.
words.ex_cn: 商店里有一个新手机的展示。
words.en: To display something means to put it in a place where people can see it easily, or to show it to people.

words.ex: He wants to pursue his dream of becoming a writer.
words.ex_cn: 他想追求成为作家的梦想。
words.en: If you pursue an activity, interest, or plan, you carry it out or follow it.

words.ex: They established a new school in the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们在村里建立了一所新学校。
words.en: To set up or create something, such as an organization or a system, on a firm or permanent basis.

words.ex: His dedication to teaching helped many students succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他对教学的奉献帮助了许多学生取得成功。
words.en: The act of dedicating or the state of being dedicated; commitment.

words.ex: He felt satisfaction after finishing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他完成作业后感到满意。
words.en: The feeling of pleasure that you have when you do or get something that you wanted or needed.

words.ex: He shows a strong sense of responsibility at work.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中表现出强烈的责任感。
words.en: A sense of responsibility is a feeling that it is your duty to deal with something or to care for someone.

words.tr:
v. 适合；相配；
n. 套装；西装；诉讼；
words.ex: This color suits her well.
words.ex_cn: 这个颜色很适合她。
words.en: A suit is a set of clothes made from the same fabric, usually consisting of a jacket and trousers or a skirt. As a verb, to suit means to be appropriate or acceptable for someone or something.

words.ex: You have three options to choose from.
words.ex_cn: 你有三个选项可以选择。
words.en: An option is something that you can choose to do in preference to one or more alternatives.

words.tr: phrase. 赞成与反对；正面与反面；利弊
words.ex: We listed the pros and cons before making a decision.
words.ex_cn: 我们在做决定之前列出了利弊。
words.en: The advantages and disadvantages of something, especially something that you are considering doing.

words.ex: His pursuit of happiness made him work hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 他对幸福的追求让他每天努力工作。
words.en: The act of pursuing something or someone, especially in order to catch or achieve them.

words.ex: She tries to juggle her job and caring for her kids.
words.ex_cn: 她努力兼顾工作和照顾孩子。
words.en: If you juggle, you keep several objects in motion in the air at the same time by repeatedly throwing and catching them. Juggle can also mean to deal with several things at the same time, often in a skillful way.

words.tr:
v. 转换；
n. 开关；
words.ex: He switched off the light before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前把灯关掉了。
words.en: A switch is a small control for an electrical device which you use to turn the device on or off.

words.ex: The teacher will assess your homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会评估你的作业。
words.en: to judge or decide the amount, value, quality, or importance of something

words.ex: His loyalty to his friends never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
words.en: The quality of being loyal to someone or something.

words.tr:
adj. 最初的；开始的；
n. 首字母；
words.ex: This is the initial plan for the project.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个项目的最初计划。
words.en: The first letter of a name or word, used to represent the whole name or word.

words.tr: n. 商机；理想的工作或生活；
words.ex: He found a niche in selling eco-friendly phone cases.
words.ex_cn: 他在销售环保手机壳方面找到了商机。
words.en: A niche is a hollow area in a wall which has been made to hold a statue, or a comfortable or suitable position in life or employment.

words.tr:
n. 基础；接地；搁浅
v. 放在地上；使 ... 搁浅；禁足；于…基础上；“ground”的现在分词
words.ex: He has grounding in basic physics.
words.ex_cn: 他有基础物理的知识。
words.en: The basic knowledge or training in a particular subject or activity that is necessary before more advanced work can be done.

words.tr: phrase. v. 不赞成；反对；对…皱眉表示不满
words.ex: My parents frown upon staying up late.
words.ex_cn: 我的父母不赞成熬夜。
words.en: To disapprove of or be opposed to something.

words.ex: The exam was stressful for all students.
words.ex_cn: 这次考试对所有学生来说压力很大。
words.en: If a situation or experience is stressful, it makes you feel worried and tense because of difficulties or problems.

words.ex: He felt insecurity when he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 当他失去工作时，他感到不安全感。
words.en: Insecurity is a feeling of uncertainty or anxiety about oneself or one's situation.

words.ex: He made a permanent change to his lifestyle.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的生活方式做出了永久的改变。
words.en: Something that is permanent exists or happens all the time, or exists for a long time without changing.

words.ex: He will forego dessert to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 为了保持健康，他将放弃甜点。
words.en: To forego something means to decide not to have or do something that you would like to have or do.

words.ex: Poor hygiene can give rise to infections.
words.ex_cn: 不良的卫生习惯可能导致感染。
words.en: To cause something to happen or exist.

words.ex: He saw the mistake but decided to turn a blind eye to it.
words.ex_cn: 他看到了那个错误，但决定视而不见。
words.en: If you say that someone is turning a blind eye to something bad or illegal that is happening, you mean that you think they are pretending not to notice that it is happening so that they will not have to do anything about it.

words.tr: phrase. 渴望做某事的；急切想要做某事的
words.ex_cn: 他渴望学习英语。
words.en: If you are eager to do or have something, you want to do or have it very much.

words.ex: He wants to study journalism after high school.
words.ex_cn: 他想在高中后学习新闻工作。
words.en: The profession or practice of reporting about, photographing, or editing news stories for one of the mass media.

words.tr: phrase. 覆盖范围的文字说明；用于描述某项服务或产品覆盖区域的标注文字
words.ex: The map includes a coverage lettering that explains the service areas.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图包含了一段文字说明，解释了服务范围。
words.en: Text or lettering used to describe or provide information about an insurance policy's coverage.

words.ex: The newspaper's headline said 'City Wins Championship'.
words.ex_cn: 报纸的大字标题写着‘城市赢得冠军’。
words.en: A headline is the title of a newspaper story, printed in large letters at the top of the story, especially on the front page.

words.ex: The barometer shows that the weather will be fine.
words.ex_cn: 晴雨表显示天气会很好。
words.en: A barometer is an instrument that measures atmospheric pressure, used especially in forecasting the weather and determining altitude.

words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

words.tr: adj. 无所不在的；遍及各处的
words.ex: The smell of bread is omnipresent in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨面包的香味无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something as omnipresent, you mean that it seems to be everywhere at the same time.

words.tr: adj. 最新的；最近的；新式的
words.ex: He keeps his knowledge up-to-date by reading news every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天读新闻来保持知识的更新。
words.en: Someone or something that is up-to-date has the most recent information or uses the newest methods or equipment.

words.ex: The accident was newsworthy because many people were hurt.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故很有新闻价值，因为很多人受伤了。
words.en: If something is newsworthy, it is interesting enough to be reported as news.

words.ex: He judged the case objectively.
words.ex_cn: 他客观地评判了这个案件。
words.en: In a way that is not influenced by personal feelings or opinions.

words.ex: The letter revealed his secret.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他的秘密。
words.en: To reveal something means to make known something that was previously secret or unknown.

words.ex: He tried to cover up his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他试图掩盖自己的错误。
words.en: To conceal something, especially a mistake or a crime, by hiding it or by pretending that it does not exist.

words.tr: adj. 有偏见的； v. “bias”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The judge was biased against the defendant.
words.ex_cn: 这位法官对被告有偏见。
words.en: If someone is biased, they prefer one group of people to another, and behave unfairly as a result.

words.tr: n. 广告活动；广告业； v. 做广告；“advertise”的现在分词；
words.ex: The company launched a new advertising campaign last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司上个月推出了一项新的广告活动。
words.en: The activity of producing advertisements for commercial products or services.

words.tr:
adj. 贸易的；商业的；
n. 广告；
words.ex: The commercial ship sailed to another country.
words.ex_cn: 这艘贸易船只驶向了另一个国家。
words.en: Commercial relates to the business of buying and selling goods and services.

words.tr: adj. 非商业性的；非营利的；
words.ex: The museum is noncommercial and free for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆是非商业性的，对所有人免费。
words.en: Not involving or intended for commercial purposes.

words.ex: The painter portrays a happy family in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这位画家在画中描绘了一个幸福的家庭。
words.en: To portray someone or something means to show or represent them in a painting, film, book, or other artistic work.

words.tr: n. 定位； v. “position”的现在分词；
words.ex: The company is working on the positioning of its new product.
words.ex_cn: 公司正在研究其新产品的定位。
words.en: The act of placing or arranging something in a particular position.

words.ex: The soldiers were bombarded with cannon fire.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们遭到炮火轰击。
words.en: To bombard someone or something means to attack them continuously with bombs, shells, or other missiles. It can also mean to subject someone to a lot of something, such as questions or information.

words.tr:
v. 摇摆；摇动；
n. 影响；支配；
words.ex: The tree branches sway in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 树的枝条在风中摇摆。
words.en: To sway means to move slowly or rhythmically backwards and forwards or from side to side. It can also mean to influence someone or something.

words.ex: He squandered all his money on games.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都浪费在游戏上了。
words.en: If you squander money, resources, or opportunities, you waste them in a foolish or careless way.

words.ex: He bought the car impulsively.
words.ex_cn: 他有推动力地买了那辆车。
words.en: If you describe someone as acting impulsively, you mean that they act suddenly without thinking carefully about what they are doing, often because they are being controlled by their emotions.

words.tr:
v. 伪造；假装；冒充；
adj. 假的；冒充的；伪造的；
words.ex: He faked a signature to get the money.
words.ex_cn: 他伪造了一个签名来拿到钱。
words.en: If something is fake, it is not real, genuine, or true, but is made to appear so.

words.ex: The company made fraudulent claims about its product.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司对其产品做出了欺诈性的声明。
words.en: A fraudulent activity is deceitful or dishonest.

words.ex: He showed me the trick to solve this math problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他给我展示了快速解决这道数学题的诀窍。
words.en: A trick is a clever or deceitful action intended to deceive or outwit someone.

words.tr: adj. 未经审查的；未作删剪的
words.ex: The movie is uncensored and shows real violence.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是未删减的，展示了真实的暴力场面。
words.en: If something is uncensored, it has not been censored, and so may contain information or scenes that some people find offensive or shocking.

words.ex: His story was an exaggeration of the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事是对事实的夸张。
words.en: An exaggeration is a statement that represents something as better or worse than it really is.

words.ex: He does not want to intrude on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他不想插话他们的谈话。
words.en: To intrude means to enter somewhere or become involved in a situation where you are not wanted or are not supposed to be.

words.ex: He uses this park exclusively for walking.
words.ex_cn: 他只在这个公园散步。
words.en: If you do something exclusively, you do it only in the way mentioned, and not in any other way.

words.tr: phrase. 成天懒散在家、久坐不动看电视的人；电视迷
words.ex: He is a couch potato who watches TV all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是个整天看电视的沙发土豆。
words.en: A couch potato is a person who spends a lot of time sitting or lying down, usually watching television.

words.tr: adj. 攻击性的；有进取心的；侵略性的；
words.ex: The dog showed aggressive behavior toward strangers.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗对陌生人表现出攻击性行为。
words.en: An aggressive person or animal has a quality of anger and determination that makes them ready to attack others.

words.ex: The accident immobilised the car.
words.ex_cn: 事故使汽车无法动弹。
words.en: To prevent something or someone from moving or operating as normal.

words.tr: v. 诱捕；诱入陷阱；使入圈套
words.ex: The trap will ensnare the rabbit.
words.ex_cn: 陷阱会抓住兔子。
words.en: To catch or trap someone or something, often in a way that is deceitful or unfair.

words.ex: The thermostat helps regulate the room temperature.
words.ex_cn: 恒温器有助于调节室温。
words.en: To regulate something means to control or manage it, especially by means of rules or laws.

words.ex: The law restricts driving after drinking.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制酒后驾驶。
words.en: to limit the movements or actions of someone, or to limit something and reduce its size or prevent it from increasing

words.ex: The government imposed censorship on the news.
words.ex_cn: 政府对新闻实施了审查。
words.en: Censorship is the censoring of books, plays, films, or reports, especially by government officials, because they are considered immoral or secret in some way.

words.ex: The teacher gave supervision to the students during the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试期间监督学生。
words.en: The act of overseeing or directing a project, activity, or person.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.tr:
n. 聚光灯；
v. 使公众注意；
words.ex: The spotlight shone on the singer during the concert.
words.ex_cn: 演唱会上，聚光灯照在歌手身上。
words.en: A spotlight is a powerful light, for example in a theatre, which can be directed so that it lights up a small area. If someone or something is in the spotlight, they are getting a lot of attention from the public and the media.

chapters.name: Task 2 - 国际化与发展题材

words.ex: They have mutual respect for each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此相互尊重。
words.en: Mutual is used to describe a situation, feeling, or action that is experienced, felt, or done by each of two or more parties towards the other or others.

words.tr: n. 紧张；紧张局势；紧张关系；
words.ex: There was tension between the two friends after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 两人争吵后，彼此之间出现了紧张。
words.en: Tension is a feeling of worry and anxiety which makes it difficult for you to relax. It can also refer to the state of being stretched tight or the degree of tightness of a stretched string, wire, etc.

words.ex: The two colors are distinct.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色有区别。
words.en: If something is distinct, it is easily seen, heard, or understood.

words.tr: adj. 外来的；外国来的；奇异的；
words.ex: The market sells exotic fruits from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个市场出售来自其他国家的外来水果。
words.en: Something that is exotic is unusual and interesting because it comes from or is related to a distant country.

words.ex: The school values diversity in its students.
words.ex_cn: 学校重视学生的多样性。
words.en: The state of being diverse; variety.

words.ex: He showed his identity card to enter the building.
words.ex_cn: 他出示了身份证以进入大楼。
words.en: Your identity is who you are, or the qualities of a person or group that make them different from others.

words.ex: The fence marks the boundary between the two gardens.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏标志着两个花园的分界线。
words.en: A boundary is a real or imagined line that marks the edge or limit of something.

words.tr:
n. 展示优点的场合（或机会）；
v. 展示…的优点；
words.ex: The competition was a showcase for her talent.
words.ex_cn: 这次比赛是她展示才华的机会。
words.en: A showcase is a setting in which someone or something is displayed to its best advantage, or a glass case used for displaying articles in a shop or museum.

words.tr: n. 陷阱；隐患；想不到的困难；
words.ex: Don't ignore the pitfall of skipping homework.
words.ex_cn: 不要忽视不做作业这个陷阱。
words.en: A pitfall is a likely mistake or problem in a situation.

words.ex: The integration of technology and education improves learning.
words.ex_cn: 技术与教育的结合改善了学习。
words.en: The act or process of combining or adding parts to make a unified whole.

words.ex: He had a misapprehension about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则有一个误解。
words.en: A misapprehension is a failure to understand something correctly, often leading to a mistaken belief or idea.

words.tr: phrase. 生活标准；生活水平
words.ex: His job improved the standard of living for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他的工作改善了家人的生活水平。
words.en: The level of wealth, comfort, material goods, and necessities available to a certain socioeconomic class or a certain geographic area.

words.ex: The donor gave money to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 捐赠者向医院捐了钱。
words.en: A donor is a person or organization that gives something, especially money, to a charity or other organization.

words.tr: adj. 慈善的；乐善好施的；
words.ex: He made a philanthropic donation to help poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一笔慈善款项来帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: A philanthropic person or organization freely gives money or other help to people who need it.

words.tr: adj. 人道主义的；慈善的；
words.ex: The humanitarian aid helped the hungry children.
words.ex_cn: 人道主义援助帮助了饥饿的孩子们。
words.en: A humanitarian is someone who is involved in or connected with improving people's lives and reducing suffering.

words.ex: The doctor showed beneficence by helping the poor patient for free.
words.ex_cn: 医生通过免费帮助贫困病人展现了仁慈。
words.en: Beneficence refers to the quality or state of doing or producing good; active kindness or charity.

words.ex: He felt an obligation to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他感到有义务帮助他的朋友。
words.en: An obligation is something that you must do because you have promised, because of a law, etc.

words.ex: He wants to get rid of the old chair.
words.ex_cn: 他想扔掉那把旧椅子。
words.en: To dispose of or remove something unwanted or undesirable.

words.tr: adj. 为贫穷所困恼的，为贫穷所困扰的；非常贫穷的
words.ex: The poverty-stricken family needs food and water.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫困的家庭需要食物和水。
words.en: Extremely poor.

words.ex: The needy family received food from the charity.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫穷的家庭从慈善机构收到了食物。
words.en: Needy people do not have enough food, medicine, or clothing, or adequate houses.

words.ex: He saves money for long-term goals.
words.ex_cn: 他为长期目标存钱。
words.en: Something that is long-term has continued for a long time or will continue for a long time in the future.

words.ex: He misspent his money on video games.
words.ex_cn: 他把钱浪费在电子游戏上了。
words.en: To spend time or money in a wasteful or unwise way.

words.tr: adj. 受限制的；有限的； v. 限制；约束；“restrict”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The children have restricted screen time.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们的屏幕使用时间是受限制的。
words.en: If something is restricted, it is limited or controlled, especially by rules or laws.

words.ex: The family is in a difficult plight after losing their home.
words.ex_cn: 这家人在失去家园后陷入了困境。
words.en: A plight is a difficult or adverse situation, especially one that is hard to escape. It can also refer to a solemn promise or pledge.

words.ex: The government wants to eradicate poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消灭贫困。
words.en: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.

words.tr: n. 误解；误会； v. “misunderstand”的现在分词；
words.ex: There was a misunderstanding between them about the time.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间对时间产生了误解。
words.en: A misunderstanding is a failure to understand something correctly, often leading to confusion or disagreement.

words.tr: adj. 两种语言的；用两种语言的；
words.ex: He is a bilingual student who speaks English and Spanish.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个会说英语和西班牙语的双语学生。
words.en: A bilingual person is someone who can speak two languages equally well.

words.tr: n. 父亲的地位（或身份）
words.ex: He loves fatherhood and spends time with his kids every day.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱父亲这个角色，每天都会花时间陪孩子。
words.en: The state of being a father; the responsibilities or feelings associated with being a father.

words.tr: adj. 家庭的；国内的；驯养的；
words.ex: She prefers domestic chores over going out.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢做家务而不是外出。
words.en: Domestic means relating to the home, family, or household affairs. It can also refer to something that is made or produced within a country and not imported.

words.tr: phrase. 财务支持；经济援助
words.ex: He got financial support from his parents.
words.ex_cn: 他从父母那里获得了经济支持。
words.en: Financial support refers to the provision of money or resources to help someone or something, especially in the context of education, business, or personal needs.

words.tr: phrase. 同年龄组；同辈群体
words.ex: He cares about what his peer group thinks.
words.ex_cn: 他在乎同龄人群体的看法。
words.en: A peer group is a group of people of approximately the same age, social status, and interests.

words.ex: He will pass on the message to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他会把消息转告给他的朋友。
words.en: To give something to someone else, especially after receiving it or using it; to continue moving forward; to die.

words.ex: His comportment at the meeting was very polite.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上的举止非常礼貌。
words.en: The way in which someone behaves or conducts themselves.

words.ex: The dog learned through conditioning to sit when it hears a whistle.
words.ex_cn: 狗通过条件作用学会在听到口哨时坐下。
words.en: The process of training or accustoming a person or animal to behave in a certain way or to accept certain circumstances.

words.ex: Tea is preferable to coffee in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早上喝茶比喝咖啡更好。
words.en: If you say that one thing is preferable to another, you mean that it is more desirable or suitable.

words.ex: He had to resort to asking for help.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不求助于别人。
words.en: If you resort to a particular course of action, you do it because other methods have failed.

words.ex: They felt a strong kinship because they grew up in the same village.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为从小在同一个村庄长大，感到有很强的亲属关系。
words.en: Kinship is the relationship between members of the same family.

words.tr: phrase. 核心家庭（只包括父母和子女的家庭）
words.ex: He lives with his parents and sister in a nuclear family.
words.ex_cn: 他和父母及妹妹生活在一个核心家庭中。
words.en: A nuclear family is a family group consisting of two parents and their children.

words.tr: phrase. 大家庭；扩大的家庭（如数代同堂的家庭）
words.ex: He lives with his extended family in a big house.
words.ex_cn: 他和大家庭住在一起，住在一所大房子里。
words.en: A family group that consists of parents, children, and other close relatives, often living in close proximity.

words.tr: phrase. 代沟；指不同世代之间在思想、价值观或行为方式上的差异
words.ex: Parents and children often disagree because of the generation gap.
words.ex_cn: 父母和孩子经常因为代沟而产生分歧。
words.en: A generation gap is a difference in attitudes, behaviors, and preferences between people of different generations, often leading to a lack of understanding or conflict.

words.ex: The program helps intergenerational families share stories.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目帮助代际家庭分享故事。
words.en: Relating to or involving different generations, especially in families or societies.

words.tr: n. 养老金；退休金；抚恤金；
words.ex: He receives a monthly pension after retiring.
words.ex_cn: 他退休后每月领取养老金。
words.en: A pension is a sum of money which a retired, widowed, or disabled person regularly receives from the state or from a former employer.

words.ex: He tried to reconcile his work and family life.
words.ex_cn: 他试图调和工作与家庭生活。
words.en: If you reconcile two beliefs, facts, or demands that seem to be opposed or completely different, you find a way in which they can both be true or both be successful.

words.ex: There is friction between the two neighbors over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居因为篱笆问题产生了不和。
words.en: The resistance that one surface or object encounters when moving over another.

words.ex: The obedient child cleaned his room without being told.
words.ex_cn: 这个听话的孩子没被要求就打扫了房间。
words.en: An obedient person or animal does what they are told to do.

words.tr: adj. 私下参与的；私下的；秘密的
words.ex: He is privy to the secret plan.
words.ex_cn: 他知道这个秘密计划。
words.en: If you are privy to something secret, you have been allowed to know about it.

words.tr: adj. 自我中心的；自私自利的
words.ex: He is egoistic and only thinks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他很自私，只考虑自己。
words.en: Egoistic refers to someone who is excessively self-centered or self-interested.

words.ex: The teacher was fired for misconduct.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师因行为不端被解雇了。
words.en: Misconduct refers to unacceptable or improper behavior, especially by a professional person.

words.ex: The rebellious boy refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个叛逆的男孩拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you think someone is rebellious, you mean that they are deliberately not obeying people in authority or rules of behaviour.

words.tr:
n. 方面；尊重；尊敬；
v. 遵从；尊重；尊敬；
words.ex: In this respect, the plan is good.
words.ex_cn: 在这个方面，这个计划很好。
words.en: If you respect someone, you have a good opinion of their character or ideas.

words.ex: The scientist studied genetic traits in plants.
words.ex_cn: 科学家研究了植物的基因特征。
words.en: relating to genes or heredity

words.ex: He inherited a house from his father.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一所房子。
words.en: If you inherit something such as a trait, characteristic, or quality, you are born with it, because your parents or ancestors had it. If you inherit money or property, you receive it from someone who has died.

words.ex: Honesty is a good trait.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种好的特性。
words.en: A trait is a particular characteristic, quality, or tendency that someone or something has.

words.ex: The birth rate in this country is falling.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的出生率正在下降。
words.en: The birth rate is the number of live births per thousand of population per year.

words.tr: n. 自我控制；克己； 自控力
words.ex: He showed self-control when he stayed calm.
words.ex_cn: 当他保持冷静时，他表现出了自制力。
words.en: Self-control is the ability to not show your feelings or not do the things that your feelings make you want to do.

words.ex: He plans to start his retirement next year.
words.ex_cn: 他计划明年退休。
words.en: Retirement is the period of one's life after leaving one's job and ceasing to work.

words.tr: adj. 人口统计的；人口的；
words.ex: The survey collected demographic data like age and income.
words.ex_cn: 这项调查收集了年龄和收入等人口统计数据。
words.en: Relating to the structure of populations.

words.tr:
adj. 资深的；高级的；年长的；
n. 年长者；大四学生；
words.ex: He is a senior engineer with 20 years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有20年经验的资深工程师。
words.en: Higher in rank, status, or importance; older in age.

words.ex: He is the breadwinner in his family.
words.ex_cn: 他是家里的经济支柱。
words.en: A breadwinner is a person who earns money to support their family.

words.tr: n. 往返移动之物；航天飞机；
words.ex: The bus is a shuttle between the hotel and the airport.
words.ex_cn: 这辆巴士是酒店和机场之间的往返交通工具。
words.en: A shuttle is a vehicle that travels frequently between two places. In weaving, a shuttle is a device used to carry the weft thread back and forth across the loom.

words.ex: The drummer changed the tempo of the song.
words.ex_cn: 鼓手改变了这首歌的拍子。
words.en: The speed at which a piece of music is played or the rate or speed of motion or activity.

words.ex: He failed the test because of lack of sleep.
words.ex_cn: 他因为缺乏睡眠而考试不及格。
words.en: The state of being without or not having enough of something.

words.tr:
n. 基金；资金；
v. 提供资金；
words.ex: The school raised a fund for new books.
words.ex_cn: 学校为购买新书筹集了一笔基金。
words.en: A sum of money saved or made available for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The price is in dispute between the buyer and seller.
words.ex_cn: 这个价格在买家和卖家之间存在争议。
words.en: If something is in dispute, people are arguing or disagreeing about it.

words.ex: He can identify the bird by its song.
words.ex_cn: 他能通过鸟的叫声识别它。
words.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.tr: n. 强迫；强制；难以抗拒的冲动
words.ex: He felt a compulsion to check the door again.
words.ex_cn: 他感到一种必须再次检查门的强迫感。
words.en: A compulsion is a very strong desire to do something, which you find difficult to control.

words.tr:
adj. 中途的；中间的
adv. 中途地；中间地
n. 娱乐场；游乐场
words.ex: He stopped midway to rest.
words.ex_cn: 他中途停下来休息。
words.en: Midway is used to describe something that is in the middle of a place or a period of time.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet is a preventive measure.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔是一种预防性的措施。
words.en: Designed to stop something undesirable from occurring.

words.ex: Good hygiene helps prevent sickness.
words.ex_cn: 良好的卫生有助于预防疾病。
words.en: Hygiene refers to conditions and practices that help to maintain health and prevent the spread of diseases.

words.tr:
n. 预算；预算金额；
adj. 廉价的；花钱少的；
v. 为 ... 做预算；
words.ex: We made a budget for our vacation.
words.ex_cn: 我们为旅行制定了一个预算。
words.en: A budget is a plan that shows how much money a person or organization will earn and how much they will need or be able to spend.

words.tr: phrase. 呼吁；号召；要求；接（人）
words.ex: The situation calls for immediate action.
words.ex_cn: 这种情况需要立即采取行动。
words.en: If you call for something, you demand that it should happen.

words.tr:
adj. 文盲的；无知的；
n. 文盲；无知识的人；
words.ex: He is illiterate and cannot read simple signs.
words.ex_cn: 他是文盲，无法阅读简单的标识。
words.en: Someone who is illiterate cannot read or write.

words.tr: phrase. 使用；接近；可以利用
words.ex: Students have access to the library after school.
words.ex_cn: 学生放学后可以使用图书馆。
words.en: To have the right or opportunity to use or see something.

words.tr: adj. 可获得的；有空的；可用的；
words.ex: The books are available in the library.
words.ex_cn: 这些书在图书馆里可以借到。
words.en: If something is available, it is able to be used or obtained.

words.ex: He works hard for the betterment of his family.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以改善家人的生活。
words.en: The act or process of improving something or the state of being improved.

words.tr:
v. 征收；征税；征募
n. 征兵；征税
words.ex: The government will levy a new tax next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将征收一项新税。
words.en: To levy means to impose or collect a tax, fee, or fine. It can also refer to the act of enlisting or drafting individuals into military service.

words.ex: The ship carries a provision of food for the journey.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船为旅程准备了食物供应。
words.en: A provision is a condition or requirement in a legal document. It can also refer to the act of supplying or providing something that is needed.

words.ex: He rubbed his shoulder after lifting the box.
words.ex_cn: 他搬完箱子后揉了揉肩膀。
words.en: The part of the body at each side of the neck where the upper limb or forelimb is attached; to accept or take on (a responsibility or task).

words.ex: The government provides welfare to poor families.
words.ex_cn: 政府向贫困家庭提供福利。
words.en: The welfare of a person or group is their health, comfort, and happiness.

words.tr: phrase. 社会保障；社会保险
words.ex: He receives social security every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月都领取社会保障金。
words.en: A government system that provides financial assistance to people with an inadequate or no income.

words.ex: He needs better medical care after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后需要更好的医疗照顾。
words.en: The provision of what is necessary for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease and the maintenance of health.

words.tr: phrase. 健康保险；医疗保险
words.ex: He bought health insurance for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他为家人购买了医疗保险。
words.en: Health insurance is a type of insurance coverage that pays for medical and surgical expenses incurred by the insured. Health insurance can reimburse the insured for expenses incurred from illness or injury, or pay the care provider directly.

words.ex: The administrative office handles school records.
words.ex_cn: 行政办公室负责管理学校档案。
words.en: Relating to the management of a company, organization, or institution.

words.tr:
adj. 犯罪的；
n. 罪犯；
words.ex: He made a criminal mistake by stealing money.
words.ex_cn: 他偷钱犯了一个犯罪的错误。
words.en: A criminal is a person who has committed a crime.

words.ex: The city is trying to reduce juvenile delinquency with after-school programs.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市正通过课后项目来减少青少年犯罪。
words.en: Juvenile delinquency refers to the participation in illegal behavior by minors (juveniles) who fall under a statutory age limit.

words.ex: The crime rate in this city is low.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的犯罪率很低。
words.en: The crime rate is the number of crimes that are committed in a particular area during a particular period of time.

words.ex: The crime-ridden neighborhood needs more police.
words.ex_cn: 这个犯罪频发的社区需要更多警察。
words.en: An area or place that is crime-ridden has a very high level of crime.

words.tr: n. 得罪人的人；犯罪者；违法者；
words.ex: He was punished because he was an offender who hurt his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他因为是一个得罪朋友的人而受到惩罚。
words.en: An offender is a person who commits a crime or does something wrong.

words.ex: The violator must pay a fine.
words.ex_cn: 违规者必须支付罚款。
words.en: A violator is someone who breaks a law, rule, or agreement.

words.ex: The police caught the lawbreaker near the bank.
words.ex_cn: 警察在银行附近抓到了违法者。
words.en: A lawbreaker is someone who breaks the law.

words.ex: He got a fine for a small infraction.
words.ex_cn: 他因一个小违规行为被罚款。
words.en: An infraction is a violation or infringement of a law, agreement, or set of rules.

words.ex: He has a propensity for telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他有说实话的倾向。
words.en: A propensity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way.

words.tr:
adj. 不正常的；离经叛道的
n. 不正常的人
words.ex: His deviant behavior surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他不正常的行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Deviant behavior or thinking is different from what people normally consider to be acceptable.

words.ex: The new policy is problematic for small businesses.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策对小企业来说成问题。
words.en: If something is problematic, it involves problems and is difficult to deal with or solve.

words.ex: He got a penalty for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规则而受到惩罚。
words.en: A penalty is a punishment that is imposed on someone for doing something that is against the rules or the law.

words.ex: The court imposed a punitive fine for the violation.
words.ex_cn: 法院对这一违规行为处以惩罚性罚款。
words.en: Punitive actions, laws, or measures are intended to punish someone.

words.ex: He will embark on a new journey next month.
words.ex_cn: 他下个月将开始一段新的旅程。
words.en: To start or begin something, especially something new, challenging, or exciting.

words.ex: He did an unlawful act and was arrested.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一件非法的事，被逮捕了。
words.en: If something is unlawful, it is against the law.

words.ex: He hired a legal lawyer to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他请了一位法律律师来帮助他。
words.en: Relating to the law or to lawyers, or permitted or required by law.

words.ex: The boy was punished for his misdeed.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因他的恶劣行为而受到惩罚。
words.en: A misdeed is a wrong or illegal deed; a crime or sin.

words.tr: n. 轻罪；品行不端；轻刑罪
words.ex: He committed a misdemeanor by parking illegally.
words.ex_cn: 他因非法停车而犯下轻罪。
words.en: A misdemeanor is a less serious crime than a felony, punishable by less than a year of imprisonment.

words.ex: This sentence is easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这个句子很容易理解。
words.en: A sentence is a group of words which, when they are written down, begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop, question mark, or exclamation mark. Most sentences contain a subject and a verb.

words.tr:
v. 非法侵入；侵扰；冒犯
n. 非法进入；冒犯
words.ex: He trespasses on private land.
words.ex_cn: 他擅自进入私人土地。
words.en: To trespass is to enter someone's land or property without their permission.

words.tr: n. 违反（法规、规章制度等）；侵犯（合法权益）
words.ex: The company faced a lawsuit for copyright infringement.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司因侵犯版权而面临诉讼。
words.en: An infringement is an action that breaks a rule, law, etc.

words.ex: He was jailed for embezzlement from his company.
words.ex_cn: 他因盗用公司公款而入狱。
words.en: Embezzlement is the act of dishonestly taking or using money that belongs to someone else, especially when it is in your care or belongs to the organization you work for.

words.tr: phrase. 执法；法律的执行；执法机构（统称）
words.ex: The law enforcement officers caught the thief.
words.ex_cn: 执法人员抓到了小偷。
words.en: The action or process of enforcing laws, especially by the police or other authorities.

words.ex: The city passed an ordinance to stop littering.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市通过了一项禁止乱扔垃圾的法令。
words.en: An ordinance is an authoritative rule, law, decree, or command.

words.ex: He is in rehabilitation after his surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他术后正在康复。
words.en: Rehabilitation is the process of helping someone to have a normal, useful life again after they have been very ill or in prison, or the process of returning a building or area to its previous good condition.

words.tr: n. 依恋；附件；附加装置；
words.ex: The child showed strong attachment to his teddy bear.
words.ex_cn: 孩子对他的泰迪熊产生了强烈的依恋。
words.en: An attachment is a file that is sent along with an email message.

words.ex: He engages in sports after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后参加体育运动。
words.en: To participate or become involved in an activity.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.tr: adj. 隐藏的； v. 隐藏；“hide”的过去分词；
words.ex: The keys are hidden under the mat.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙藏在垫子下面。
words.en: If something is hidden, it is not easily noticed or found.

words.ex: The teacher made an intervention to help the student.
words.ex_cn: 老师进行了干预以帮助学生。
words.en: Intervention is the act of intervening, especially in a situation to prevent something undesirable from happening.

words.tr: adj. 无结果的；无成效的；
words.ex: The meeting was fruitless because no decisions were made.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议毫无结果，因为没有做出任何决定。
words.en: If an action or attempt to do something is fruitless, it is unsuccessful or produces nothing of value.

words.tr: adj. 使人畏缩的；吓人的； v. “daunt”的现在分词；
words.ex: The math test seemed daunting to him.
words.ex_cn: 这次数学考试让他感到畏缩。
words.en: Something that is daunting makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.ex: Some countries still use the death penalty.
words.ex_cn: 一些国家仍然使用死刑。
words.en: The death penalty is the legally authorized killing of someone as punishment for a crime.

words.ex: His refusal to listen is irrational.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝倾听是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings and behavior as irrational, you mean they are not based on logical reasons or clear thinking.

words.ex: The smoke caused an exacerbation of his asthma.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾加重了他的哮喘。
words.en: An exacerbation is an increase in the severity of a disease or any of its symptoms.

words.tr: adj. 预谋的；事先策划的； v. “premeditate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The theft was premeditated, not random.
words.ex_cn: 这次盗窃是预谋的，不是随机的。
words.en: If you describe an action as premeditated, you mean that it has been planned or thought about before it is done.

words.tr: adj. 人道的；仁慈的；人文的
words.ex: The shelter treats animals in a humane way.
words.ex_cn: 这个收容所以人道的方式对待动物。
words.en: If you describe something as humane, you mean that it is good and kind, especially because it decreases suffering.

words.ex: The company follows ethical practices in hiring.
words.ex_cn: 该公司在招聘中遵循伦理规范。
words.en: Relating to moral principles or the branch of knowledge dealing with these.

words.ex: The barbaric act shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个野蛮的行为震惊了所有人。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as barbaric, you mean that it is extremely cruel or uncivilized.

words.tr:
n. 亡命之徒；逃犯；被剥夺法律权益者
v. 宣布…为非法；使…成为非法
words.ex: The police caught the outlaw last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚抓住了那个不法之徒。
words.en: An outlaw is a person who has broken the law and who is hiding or running away to avoid punishment. To outlaw something means to make it illegal.

words.ex: The lion lived in captivity for ten years.
words.ex_cn: 这只狮子被关押了十年。
words.en: The state of being imprisoned or confined.

words.ex: He was accused of poaching ideas from his colleague.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控盗用同事的想法。
words.en: To poach means to illegally hunt or catch animals or fish, or to cook something such as an egg without its shell in or over boiling water.

words.tr:
n. 违背；
v. 攻破；
words.ex: The company committed a breach of contract.
words.ex_cn: 该公司违反了合同。
words.en: A breach of a law, rule, or agreement is an act of breaking it.

words.tr: adj. 濒临灭绝的；有灭绝危险的； v. “endanger”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The panda is an endangered animal.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫是一种濒临灭绝的动物。
words.en: An animal or plant that is endangered is in danger of becoming extinct.

words.ex: Pandas are endangered species.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫是濒危物种。
words.en: An endangered species is a type of organism that is at risk of extinction due to a rapid decrease in its population or a loss of its critical habitat.

words.ex: He got a vaccine last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周打了疫苗。
words.en: A vaccine is a substance containing a virus or bacterium in a form that is not harmful, given to a person or animal to prevent them from getting the disease that the virus or bacterium causes.

words.tr: n. 繁殖；饲养； v. “breed”的现在分词；
words.ex: The farm focuses on cattle breeding.
words.ex_cn: 这个农场专注于牛的繁殖。
words.en: The process of producing animals or plants by sexual reproduction, or the process of raising animals or plants in controlled conditions.

words.tr:
n. 模型；模特；模范；型号；
v. 将…做成模型；当模特；
words.ex: The architect built a model of the new building.
words.ex_cn: 建筑师制作了新大楼的模型。
words.en: A model is a person whose job is to wear and show new styles of clothes and other products, or a representation of something, often on a smaller scale, or a particular design or type of product.

words.ex: He opposes vivisection because it hurts animals.
words.ex_cn: 他反对活体解剖，因为这会伤害动物。
words.en: The practice of performing operations on live animals for the purpose of experimentation or scientific research (often considered to be cruel).

words.ex: The school prohibits students from using phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If a law or someone in authority prohibits something, they forbid it or make it illegal.

words.tr: adj. 灭绝的；熄灭的；绝种的；
words.ex: The dodo is an extinct bird.
words.ex_cn: 渡渡鸟是一种灭绝的鸟。
words.en: If a species of animals or plants is extinct, it no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

words.ex: The encroachment of the desert is destroying farmland.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的侵蚀正在摧毁农田。
words.en: Encroachment refers to the act of gradually taking something, especially someone else's rights or property, without permission.

words.ex: Many old traditions die out over time.
words.ex_cn: 许多古老的传统随着时间推移而消失。
words.en: If something dies out, it becomes less and less common and eventually disappears completely.

words.ex: The accident caused severe mutilation of his hand.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故导致他的手严重切断。
words.en: The act of damaging someone's body, especially by cutting off or damaging a part of it.

words.ex: Humans domesticated dogs thousands of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 人类几千年前就驯养了狗。
words.en: To domesticate an animal or plant means to bring it under human control in order to provide food, power, or company.

words.ex: The movie was tame and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影枯燥无味。
words.en: If you describe an animal as tame, you mean that it is not afraid of humans and is not dangerous. If you describe a person or their behavior as tame, you mean that they are not very exciting or interesting.

words.ex: He felt sadness after the abandonment of his old dream.
words.ex_cn: 在放弃旧梦想后，他感到悲伤。
words.en: The act of giving up or leaving something or someone permanently.
